verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: The full cable routing is documented with color-coded annotation lines across six photos: (1) Page 13 (img-028): rooftop start — orange (AC cable), purple (AC earthing), green (DC earthing) lines originate from the panel area at the roof, with 'LA' marker at proposed lightning arrestor. (2) Page 14 (img-031): terrace level — same three color lines run horizontally behind the LG AC outdoor unit. (3) Page 14 (img-033): terrace parapet wall — lines enter a vertical cable tray/duct running down the building exterior. (4) Page 14 (img-030): terrace-floor room — green and purple lines enter via the ceiling/top opening and route to wall-mounted 'ENPHASE ACCESSORIES BOX'. (5) Page 15 (img-034): basement electrical room — orange and green lines run horizontally along the upper beam/ceiling, turning to terminate at 'MAIN METER' (red) and 'SOLAR METER' (blue) locations; purple line also terminates at solar meter. (6) Page 16 (img-036): basement parking — green (AC earth) and orange (LA) lines continue to 'AC Earth Pit', 'DC Earth Pit', and 'LA Pit' locations. CONTINUITY: The route is traced end-to-end from roof to earth pits without orphan ends. NOTE: This is an Enphase microinverter (IQ Series) system — there is no separate DCDB; each microinverter outputs AC directly to the combiner/IQ Gateway (ACDB). The path is: Micro-inverters (under panels) → AC cables → Enphase accessories box (terrace room) → AC cable → solar meter → main panel. CONDUIT/PROTECTION: The horizontal exposed run at terrace level behind the AC unit (img-031, page 14) shows cable lines running without visible conduit, cable-tray, or clips in the photo. The vertical duct run (img-033, page 15) uses the existing building electrical duct. The roof section (img-028) does not show physical conduit on the tiled roof surface. These exposed sections require physical inspection to confirm adequate cable protection.
verdicts.rationale: The cable routing documentation covers the full end-to-end path across six annotated photos with consistent color-coding and no orphan ends; however, the horizontal exposed terrace-level run (img-031, page 14) and the tiled roof section (img-028, page 13) lack visible conduit or cable-clipping evidence in the photos, requiring physical inspection to confirm compliant cable management on these exposed sections.
